messages.author: cffcce570e30f29d
messages.subject: creating a RDump file for CmdStan
parts:
Hi All

Here is my code for creating an RDump file from a R file (see the code in bold below)


dat_rstn =
  list(N = N, K = K, D = D, J = J, I = I, # dimensions
       y = dat_choice[['choice']],            # choices = dependent variable
       id = dat_choice[['id']],                  # household ids
       x = x_arr,                                   # design matrix
       d = dem)                                    # group level predictors - not used, therefore 1

y  <- dat_choice[['choice']]
id <- dat_choice[['id']]

stan_rdump(list('N', 'K', 'D', 'J', 'I', 'y', 'id', 'x_arr', 'dem'), file='hbvdgsw.Rdump')

I compiled the model successfully. When I submit the following command >hbvdgsw sample data file=hbvdgsw.RDump

I get the folliowing error in CmdStan:


C:\cmdstan-2.12.0\examples\data>hbvdgsw sample data file=hbvdgsw.RDump

Exception: variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=y; base type=int
Diagnostic information:
Dynamic exception type: std::runtime_error
std::exception::what: variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=y; base type=int


What am I doing wrong in creating the RDump file? Or in the Cmdstan execution?

Krishna

messages.subject: Re: creating a RDump file for CmdStan

On Monday, October 17, 2016 at 6:18:36 PM UTC-4, krishna mohan wrote:
What am I doing wrong in creating the RDump file? Or in the Cmdstan execution?

I think you need

stan_rdump(c('N', 'K', 'D', 'J', 'I', 'y', 'id', 'x_arr', 'dem'), file='hbvdgsw.Rdump',
           envir = as.environment(dat_rstn))

Ben

messages.author: cffcce570e30f29d
messages.subject: Re: creating a RDump file for CmdStan
parts:
Thanks Ben. I have already examined the warnings documentation (which as a beginner user of RStan I do not find it to be useful - it is too brief in my naive opinion). I stopped panicking and began looking at my stan file.(see below). The message said that if L is covariance matrix then it should not be a big concern. As you can see below, L represents the cholesky factor covariance matrix. I also checked the output.csv file and I verified the coefficients generated.

My apologies for not doing the due diligence on my part with patience.

Krishna

data {
  int<lower=1> N;                                 // number of choice sets
  int<lower=1> K;                                 // number of parameters (utility)
  int<lower=1> D;                                 // number of parameters (beta)
  int<lower=2> J;                                 // number of alternatives
  int<lower=1> I;                                 // number of respondents
  int<lower=1,upper=J> y[N];                      // alternative selected
  int<lower=1,upper=I> id[N];                     // respondent index
  matrix[J,K] x[N];                               // array of design matrices
  matrix[I,D] d;                                  // matrix of demographics
}

parameters {
  matrix[D, K] mu;                                // means for beta
  matrix[K, I] alpha;                             // std normal draws
  cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega;                // cholesky factors
  vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[K] tau_unif;
}

transformed parameters {
  matrix[I,K] beta;                               // utility parameters (individual level)
  cholesky_factor_cov[K] L;                       // cholesky factors
  vector[J] v[N];                                 // utility vector for each choice set
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;                         // scale

  for (k in 1:K) tau[k] = 2.5 * tan(tau_unif[k]);

  L = diag_pre_multiply(tau, L_Omega);

  beta = d * mu + (L * alpha)';                   // individual level parameters

  for (n in 1:N) {
    v[n] = x[n] * beta[id[n]]';
  }
}

model {
  to_vector(alpha) ~ normal(0, 1);
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);                 // lkj prior
  to_vector(mu) ~ normal(0, 10);                  // prior for mean parameters

  for (n in 1:N) {
    y[n] ~ categorical_logit(v[n]);
  }
}

generated quantities {
  cov_matrix[K] Sigma;                            // cov matrix
  real<upper=0> log_lik;                          // log_lik for each sample

  Sigma = tcrossprod(L);

  log_lik = 0;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    log_lik = log_lik + categorical_logit_lpmf(y[n] | v[n]);

}

On Tuesday, October 18, 2016 at 12:53:46 AM UTC-4, krishna mohan wrote:
"validate transformed params: L is 0, but must be > 0!"

I have lots of questions: What is causing that error? Is it a serious error? How can I overcome it? Why doesn't RStan give this error but CmdStan does?

http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#exception-hamiltonian-proposal-rejected

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] creating a RDump file for CmdStan
parts:
That turns off the positive-definiteness check for L
which would otherwise be run at the end of the transformed
parameters block.

This behavior doesn't vary between CmdStan and RStan. The
language itself works exactly the same way across platforms.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: creating a RDump file for CmdStan
parts:
The parameters block needs the constraints. Every
model should have finite log density (i.e., non-zero density)
for every value of the parameters that satisfy the declared
constraints.

- Bob
